phrases: Preserving stored mechanical parameters and their original evidence.
Reading declared modular index-space cardinalities without payload arrays.

original_attempts: Public pilot: 11 pass, five wrong expected diagnostic-class failures, stopped at maxfail. ArgDigest correctly raised the catalog choice error.
Directed: 69 pass, three fixture mismatches: projecting an unsupported synthetic assignment, context-manager syntax unsupported by the public Iterator, and a nonexistent count convenience method.
Corrected directed: 77 pass with actual prepared-system projection and the documented iterator/count APIs.
Integrated: 1,616 pass, one obsolete expected refusal for a now-supported single mechanical provider. The corrected assertion checks independent preservation, not a weaker no-exception result.

Unknown-report negative: six independent projection cases fail; four expose missing keys and two accept unknown future schema labels. Scientific export was not reached in those original loop-based cases. The final twelve cases test export and projection independently.
Subsequent consumer selection: 108 pass and fourteen fast gates.

Calculation pilot: 96 pass, one test mistakenly indexes the public charge quantity as a dictionary. Corrected explicit charge-unit observation: 101 pass, including both modular roots in streamed-force controls.
acceptance: Explicit format_version selects experimental 0.6 in write/write_layers/convert; default 0.5 and its missing-mechanics encoding remain unchanged. Invalid choices are handled through ArgDigest/SMonitor.

Public full/layer reads, root recognition, legacy-handler refusal, scoped parameter/geometry queries, structural iteration and metadata cardinalities support 0.6 without pretending the legacy handler supports it.

Geometry queries/iterations do not decode unrequested mechanics; mechanical queries do not read unrelated native domains or coordinates. Mechanical-domain loading is resident, not a constant-memory column API.

Declared identity graphs, independent atom counts, chemical formal charge versus legacy mechanical formal charge, absent/default-empty/report-only/present-empty semantics and old-format upgrades are guarded.

Byte copies retain the source file; selected extraction preserves 0.6 and remaps known reports/analyses. Actual complete/reordered/complementary-file prepared systems preserve values, original reports, state bindings and selected export bytes.

Three public and three private fresh readers retain another unit policy, original producers, selected exports and actual edit invalidation with RDKit/OpenMM/Ackredit unavailable. Public cases additionally use general conversion in the fresh reader.

Known charge/type report contracts are required only at scientific-use/projection boundaries. Unknown/incomplete reports remain transportable but receive structural diagnostics rather than missing-key errors, accidental future-schema acceptance or rebinding.

Shared versioned calculation chemistry supports file inputs and preserves explicitly requested mechanical model context. Both modular roots pass the existing streamed-force and explicit-model controls; no new force algorithm or scientific model is introduced.

Clean source passes 1,843 affected cases without omissions, fourteen fast gates and fresh HTML. Five rendered pages and the API anchor are inspected; unchanged course code/outputs and six baseline warnings are retained.
limits: #256 remains open. P5 retains independent DockingMT reference-workflow/installed-client acceptance; P6 retains bounded memory/storage benchmarks, schema/default-writer freeze and first stable H5MSM 1.0 qualification.
Experimental schema support is not a tag, package, release, promotion, complete external-engine checkpoint or certification of stored assignments.
Subset conversion can load complete source domains; mechanics queries read the full static mechanical domain. Unsupported independent-layer resident compositions and legacy-handler requests refuse.

Append remains topology-free and interaction-free, validates before resizing and is not crash transactional. New 0.6 file publication requires hard links and provides atomic visibility, not crash durability.
Earlier failed attempts remain failures. The original progress weights, graphical intents and supplemental closure count receive no extra credit for this added format scope.

The previous two-worker broad selection peaked near 1.7 GiB with no pressure/OOM events; final broad testing keeps two CPUs but raises its enforced ceiling to 3 GiB. Other final jobs retain individual 2 GiB limits, one computational thread per native backend, host monitoring and the shared reserve.
